Purpose and exclusions

Local screen/observer WBP_Equipment. Show authoritative results; never store canonical gameplay quantities.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Content Browser > Add > User Interface > Widget Blueprint > User Widget. Name WBP_Equipment under Content/Game/UI.
  2. Designer: use a size-constrained root panel, heading, status text, scrolling content, primary/cancel buttons and explicit focus order. Use TextBlock/FText, not untrusted rich HTML.
  3. Graph: on owner/model injection subscribe once to its result/change delegate, then immediately refresh. On Destruct or owner replacement unbind and clear references.
  4. Button OnClicked invokes the linked custom request command; show Pending and disable duplicate submissions until the same command resolves. Display stable localized rejection text and restore focus to originating control.
  5. Create through URPGScreenRouter with the local controller as Owning Player; Add to Viewport only locally. Opening this screen does not pause a shared zone.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Functions, commands and event bindings

Project custom contracts are not engine/plugin nodes. A read-only asset participates through its consumer; it does not inherit that consumer’s mutation methods. Backend endpoint pages label transport proposals explicitly.

ContractExecution / effect
RequestEquip(CommandId, OwnedItemId, DestinationSlot, ExpectedRevision) -> Equipped|RequirementsFailed|EquipmentConflict|NoSpaceLocal only; request asynchronous owner command, observe matching result, clear stale callbacks; never save or grant.
RequestUnequip(CommandId, Slot, ExpectedItemId) -> Unequipped|NoSpace|StaleItemLocal only; request asynchronous owner command, observe matching result, clear stale callbacks; never save or grant.
ResolveEquipmentVisuals(EquippedSnapshot, ActionPage) -> LayerSet|Fallback; cosmetic onlyLocal only; request asynchronous owner command, observe matching result, clear stale callbacks; never save or grant.
RebuildEquipmentModifiers(EquipmentRevision) -> AttributesUpdated; serverLocal only; request asynchronous owner command, observe matching result, clear stale callbacks; never save or grant.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Equipment slots, two-hand conflicts and paper-doll visuals. Rule owner: URPGEquipmentComponent. This asset’s role is Local screen/observer WBP_Equipment. Show authoritative results; never store canonical gameplay quantities.

  1. Player selects owned gear and slot; UI previews compatibility but sends item identity rather than claimed stat bonuses.
  2. Backend validates ownership, class/level, slot type, binding and equipment state under the current session/revision.
  3. For a two-handed weapon, plan removal of OffHand and any replaced MainHand into the bag before commit. Reject NoSpace when displaced gear cannot fit; do not delete or silently drop it.
  4. Commit bag/equipment/binding changes and build revision together. Recompute equipment/set modifiers without accumulating duplicates.
  5. Replicate safe visual definition IDs and appearance revision to nearby clients; owner sees full stat/item details.
  6. Paper-doll resolver selects compatible action-page layers. Missing shoulder/boot/glove/chest coverage displays fallback or no overlay while valid stat bonuses remain applied.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_Rillmere / Sword_A / Shield_A / Greatblade_A / WovenCloak_A. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Equip two-hand weapon with full bag and shield equipped -> NoSpace, both current slots unchanged.
Equip shield while two-hand main weapon remains -> EquipmentConflict under initial no-auto-swap policy.
Missing visual layer -> VisualFallback warning only; stats stay active.
Sell equipped item -> reject until valid unequip or one explicitly atomic sell policy; no orphan equipment pointer.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not bind every frame, subscribe twice after possession, show Accepted before commit, trust client displayed currency or keep an old pawn reference after travel.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
